A permission set that a test assigns to the running user: grant timing by place of read. Field permission (Pf_Fld__c.Secret__c), object permission (Pf_Obj__c) and custom permission (Pf_Cust), each from its own permission set.
org: fresh scratch org from a campaign Dev Hub, Developer Edition, deleted after the run (delete verified). Org id, usernames, alias and host are not recorded.
capture date: 2026-11-16 (UTC), two repeats with identical rows. sf 2.157.8. Class source API 62.0 and 67.0 (PfA, PfS, PfT <N>), deployed at 67.0.
route: named @IsTest methods, one transaction each, one run of each class. Each method ends in System.assert(false, 'RESULT => ...') so the observation is the assertion text.
PfA: the test assigns in the method (v01 directly, v02 inside runAs(self), v03 before startTest, v04 inside startTest, v05 nested runAs, v06 unassign, v07 to another user inside runAs(self), v08 to another user directly, v09 two runAs blocks, v10 both users).
PfS: @TestSetup assigns directly. PfT: @TestSetup assigns inside runAs(self). Both run s01 to s04 (plain, with DML readers, startTest, unassign).
observation: A, D = outside any runAs (before, after); B = inside runAs(running user); C = inside runAs(other Standard User with the set assigned); X = inside the runAs block that made the assignment; E = after stopTest inside runAs. cr/rd = describe isCreateable/isAccessible, q = user-mode query, ins = insert as user, perm = FeatureManagement.checkPermission.
The administrator already holds object access on custom objects, so the object-permission rows read true in every place; they show no grant timing.

residuals.tsv (SF-5, 2026-11-16): the shapes beyond the direct reads above.
Capture: two scratch orgs, API 62.0 and 67.0, @IsTest, two repeats each; the
repeats agree. Each row is the assertion text of one method (class and method in
column 2), with its source under residuals/api62 and residuals/api67 (the
capture's own classes; the scrub's placeholder emails and defanged namespace
domains are restored). Shapes: upsert and insert of a new self assignment read
by FeatureManagement.checkPermission, a stripInaccessible read and a user-mode
query; plain and nested System.runAs(Version); Queueable, future and Batch jobs
started after the assignment; a Flow $Permission formula; Approval.lock; a mixed
List insert with the assignment last; UserRecordAccess for an assigned user;
and a 5000-row assignment insert.

Native answers these rows added (Glade now matches them): an upsert of a new
assignment is hidden like an insert; a Queueable, future or Batch job does not
see the assignment; a Version block, plain or holding a runAs of the running
user, neither sees it nor unlocks it; a Flow formula reads false until a later
runAs; a list insert with the assignment last is hidden; a partial Approval.lock
after the insert returns a failed LockResult (MIXED_DML_OPERATION); at API 62.0
a partial list insert reports the mixed-DML row error without the exception
wrapper; a UserRecordAccess read counts the assignment at once and returns rows
for a named limited user on a custom object; String.valueOf of a PageReference
is System.PageReference[url]. At API 62.0 a user's own assignment inside its
runAs block is hidden from that block; at 67.0 that insert is denied.

Not observed, so base behavior: the rendered Visualforce $Permission value
(getContent is forbidden in a test, native "Methods defined as TestMethod do not
support getContent call"); RequestVersion (not supported from an unmanaged
namespace); any approval-process behavior beyond the lock rows; update and
delete of an assignment; groups; the timing value (the row masks milliseconds;
native took 31 to 67 seconds, a measurement, not a contract).
Glade note: the timing row runs without the strict heap walk, which costs
minutes over its 5000-row nested loop.
